task.question: In art, which artist accused Devon Rodriguez of presenting his work as his own in June 2026?

Rodriguez summarily removes his social media post introducing the work as his own.

[Devon Rodriguez] Devon Rodriguez (born April 8, 1996) is an American artist from New York City. He initially gained recognition for drawing a series of realistic portraits of commuters on the New York City Subway. In 2019, Rodriguez was a finalist in the Outwin Boochever Portrait Competition for his portrait of sculptor John Ahearn. In 2020, he joined the video hosting platform TikTok and quickly achieved a large following for quick-sketching commuters and capturing their reactions when the sketches were handed to them. Rodriguez is now the most followed visual artist on the platform.

[FAQ: Why Zverev's rise to world No. 1 provokes mixed feelings] On Monday, following a breakthrough season, Alexander Zverev became the world No. 1 for the first time in his career. Zverev is the 30th man in ATP history to reach the milestone since rankings began in 1973. At 29, he is the second-oldest man to make his debut atop the rankings. And, having clinched the year-end top spot as well, he is the fourth active male player -- joining Novak Djokovic , Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner -- to do so, and the first German man. Taking over the No. 1 position, following a semifinal run at the Vienna Open, was merely a formality. His rise had been determined in October, when Sinner announced he had finished his season because of injury. "Knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," Zverev said previously. "So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal." Although there is no disputing Zverev's success this past season, for many tennis fans his achievement remains marred by two previous public allegations of domestic violence. Zverev has consistently denied the allegations. Here's everything to know about Zverev reaching No. 1 and his off-the-court past that clouds what otherwise would be a celebratory moment. How did he become No. 1? Zverev reached the world No. 2 ranking in 2022 and has long been considered among the best in the game. But he entered the 2026 season ranked No. 3, with an 0-3 record in major finals and a lopsided losing record against Sinner and Alcaraz. Because Sinner and Alcaraz had combined to win every Slam title in 2024 and 2025, few predicted Zverev would find a way to close the ranking deficit during the new season. But, despite not winning a title all year before the French Open, Zverev won at Roland Garros. During a chaotic tournament, which saw Alcaraz, the defending champion, withdraw with injury beforehand and Sinner lose in a shocking second-round upset, Zverev stayed the course when many of the other top seeds fell. In the final, Zverev held off Flavio Cobolli in five sets to claim his first major title. Alcaraz remained out through Wimbledon, and Zverev seized on his absence to reach his first final. He lost to Sinner but climbed back to No. 2 with the result. After early exits in both of his hard-court lead-in events, Zverev entered the US Open as the top seed for the first time in his Slam career, as Sinner withdrew with injury. After Alcaraz, in his first tournament back, was eliminated in the fourth round, Zverev became the de facto favorite, and he capitalized again. He defeated Ben Shelton in four convincing sets to claim his second Slam trophy. Sinner still had an 1,810-point lead in the rankings after the US Open.
